entities.summary: Lambertus Jozef (Bert) Bakker was a Dutch writer and publisher in the Netherlands. He wrote literary studies, two novels, poetry, and children's books. In World War II he was involved in the Dutch Resistance and assisted in the publication of Vrij Nederland. After the war he founded a publishing company under his own name; his nephew, also named Bert Bakker, ran the company until 1993. In 1953 he founded the literary magazine Maatstaf, which he edited until 1969. He was described as a "living legend" in the Dutch publishing industry, having supported and published authors such as Adriaan Roland Holst, Martinus Nijhoff, Gerrit Achterberg, and Neeltje Maria Min.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Bert Bakker's involvement in the Dutch Resistance and his publication of Vrij Nederland during World War II had a significant impact on the country's literary scene. His support for notable authors like Adriaan Roland Holst, Martinus Nijhoff, Gerrit Achterberg, and Neeltje Maria Min helped shape the post-war Dutch publishing industry.
